cues.speaker: wil_fenn
cues.text: Again. Double or nothing, Mistress Mossfoot.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Tam, please. 'Mistress' makes me sound like I own a boot shop.

cues.speaker: wil_fenn
cues.text: I've watched your hands the whole time. You can't cheat if I'm watching.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Cheat? Me? I once beat a river captain using nothing but my honest face.
The Crown card leaves Tamsin's sleeve and arrives in her hand. Wil, watching very closely, sees nothing at all.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Lantern and Crown. That's the hand, I'm afraid.

cues.speaker: wil_fenn
cues.text: Eight blind! That was my honey-cake money.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: ...Here. Have a honey cake. Don't tell anyone I'm soft.

cues.speaker: wil_fenn
cues.text: A soldier's riding through tonight. Fort Harrow colours. I'm going to ask him to take me with him.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: A soldier. Lovely. I'll be sure to be somewhere else.

cues.speaker: maddy_fenn
cues.text: Two candles already, and the night's barely started. Who's paying for those, the Eight?

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: The Order of Lamplighters, Mistress Fenn. I will sign for them. I always sign for things.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: Here. Lantern thirty-seven, trimmed on the twenty-second of Harvestmoon. And again on the first of Emberfall.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: A lantern is trimmed once a year. And that mark is no warden's I know. I know all of them.

cues.speaker: maddy_fenn
cues.text: Is that bad? You've got the face my Wil makes before he tells me he's broken something.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: It is... irregular. I wrote it down.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: Hold the light. Hold the road. Hold on to each other.

cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown
cues.text: Very good. Better than me; I always rush the middle part. Here, child. Hold out your hand.

cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown
cues.text: My sun-disc. Forty years round my neck. It's done more praying than I have.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: Father, I can't take this. It's yours.

cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown
cues.text: The open hand holds more than the fist. Take it. My knees have earned the rest.
A dwarf in a soldier's coat comes up the east road. He stops at the alms box, drops a coin, and says nothing.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: You're the one who leaves silver and never stays for the hymn.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Didn't think anyone noticed.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: I count the box every night. Silver doesn't come often. What's your name?

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Brannoc. Dispatches for Fort Harrow. Gone by morning.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: Oriel. Light on your road, Brannoc.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: And on yours.
The brass button on Oriel's collar catches the last of the sun. Father Tobin looks at it a moment too long.

cues.speaker: wil_fenn
cues.text: Sir! You're from Fort Harrow? I can carry a pike. I've practised with a broom.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Go home, lad. Your mother's looking for you.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Listen to the Big Man, Sprout. He's got a face like a locked door.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: And you are?

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Tam Mossfoot. Card player, storyteller, honest woman.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: She won every hand the boy played at the well. Every one. Statistically, that is remarkable.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Professor! You were counting my cards from across the square? I'm flattered.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: Everyone's welcome in the square. Even card players. What's your name? Your real one?

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: That was my real one, Sunshine. Cross my heart.
On the south road, Lantern Thirty-Seven gutters once. Then the road is dark.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: Did you feel that? Like a candle going out in my chest.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: A lantern cannot simply go out. That one has burned for three hundred years.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Quiet. Something on the road.
Brannoc stares into the dark and sees only dark. By the time the shapes have edges, they are already running.

cues.speaker: wil_fenn
cues.text: Goblins! Mam! MAM!

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: Four goblins. One road. One of me. Fine. Get behind the shield.

battle_narration.text: The goblins are fast and they are hungry, and they have already picked the one in the robes.
Brannoc's first swing ends the first goblin. He does not look at it twice.
The second dagger finds its mark. Ilsevel folds into the dust without a sound.
Tamsin's arrow takes the last runt in the shoulder. He drops, still breathing.

cues.text: Then it is quiet. Three goblins will not get up. The fourth is breathing. So, barely, is Ilsevel.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: Ilsevel! Stay with me. Aurelan, if you're listening, now would be good.
Warm light runs from Oriel's hands into Ilsevel like water into dry ground. Ilsevel's eyes open.

cues.speaker: ilsevel
cues.text: I am... technically fine. I would like it recorded that I was stabbed. Twice.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Recorded, Professor. Very brave. Mostly with your face.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: This one's alive. Small. Tie him up. Someone will want to ask him questions.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Do goblins carry coin? Asking for the village. Purely civic interest.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: He's bleeding. Hold the lamp closer, Brannoc. Nobody dies in my square tonight.
Oriel's hands are shaking, and the bandage slips twice. The goblin lives, but only just. He won't be talking before morning.

cues.speaker: maddy_fenn
cues.text: Is it over? Who's hurt? Inside, the lot of you. There's stew on, and nobody argues with me tonight.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: You stood in front of all of us. You didn't even know our names.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: You kept them standing behind me. That's holding the line.

cues.speaker: oriel
cues.text: Then we held it together.

cues.speaker: brannoc
cues.text: ...Aye.

cues.speaker: tamsin
cues.text: Free stew, then? Lovely. I'll bring the cards.
